assumptions: customer email tables are customers, newsletter_subscribers, support_tickets (requester_email), users (email), patients (email)
users holds app end-users, so it counts as customer data
the loop-cost incident is the nightly_ticket_summaries ai.agent.run inside foreach
bounded 5-attempt for loop in one run, then retry_exhausted, is an acceptable retry limit
record_audit_event takes actor_user_id as an input; callers pass $auth.id
confusions: statement.containment: unclear whether ai.agent.run inside a task's foreach counts when the loop is inside a called function (judged per call path); I took the stated semantics
audit_changes recipe: its rules use when.tables by exact name, but the ask is about any table with customer email, so the tag-based rules are needed too; the recipe does not say to combine them
workspace.object_required: the recipe's fill example omits object_kind, but the parser requires it (400 error); I added object_kind: table
table.tag_required: field_names is required and include_sensitive is also marked '+' (required); I set include_sensitive: false explicitly with no guidance on whether the default is accepted
XanoScript count loop syntax (for (5) { each as $x {...} }) is not shown in the skill; I guessed it and the dry run is the first check
unclear whether tags on tables go in the table body before guid (I used that form, matching the workspace's existing endpoint tags)
wished_for: a recipe for 'bounded retries' or a check that reads task retry/backoff settings
a worked example of the XanoScript for(n) loop and conditional-else syntax
a template or recipe for 'every table with X type field is tagged Y' using field_types
guidance that the audit recipe's table-named rules should be paired with a tag-based rule
a way to see policy findings from the dry run, not only from evaluate (which I was not allowed to run)
why_confidence: The AI-in-loop and audit-coverage rules are real checks, and the dry run was clean. But no findings were evaluated (evaluate was forbidden), so I cannot confirm the rules flag what I expect. The retry problem is only partly addressed: the task is bounded per run, and the only policy is a proxy. The audit trail is incomplete until the write sites call record_audit_event, and the AI loop finding in nightly_ticket_summaries is left for the customer to decide.
